explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. After the grain, the new wine and the oil, the LORD says, "And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people." (Joel 2:28) Pour is a big word. I think of a whole bowl of chocolate chips going into the dough, not a sprinkle here and there.

I get why you'd go there, friend, because prophets say some heavy things. But look at where this verse sits. Right after the promise of grain, new wine and oil, the LORD says, "And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people." (Joel 2:28) The thing being poured out is His Spirit.

Judgment is a fair guess, since prophets talk about it a lot. But this verse is a different kind of pouring. The LORD says, "And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people." (Joel 2:28) Spirit is what's coming out of the pitcher here, friend.
All, baker! The LORD says, "I will pour out My Spirit on all people." (Joel 2:28) Not some people, not a few people. ALL. That's a wide-open bakery door.
Chosen sounds like it belongs, I know. But the word the LORD uses is "all." He says, "I will pour out My Spirit on all people." (Joel 2:28) There's no short guest list on this one, friend.
Holy has a nice ring to it, but it's not in the verse. The LORD says, "I will pour out My Spirit on all people." (Joel 2:28) No test at the door. The word is "all."

Careful, friend, because the verse says the opposite. The LORD says, "Your sons and daughters will prophesy." (Joel 2:28) Sons AND daughters. Nobody gets left standing at the counter with an empty apron.

False is right, baker. The LORD says, "Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions." (Joel 2:28) Daughters are right there next to the sons. Everybody gets a turn at the dough.

Yes, baker! The LORD says, "Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days." (Joel 2:29) Servants are the ones you'd expect to be last in line. Here they get the Spirit poured out on them too. I love that, friend.

Kings and princes feel like the natural next guess, I'll give you that. But the verse goes another direction. The LORD says, "Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days." (Joel 2:29) That's the "even" moment, friend.

Priests and Levites are a smart guess, since they served in the temple. But the verse doesn't name them here. The LORD says, "Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days." (Joel 2:29) Servants are the ones He names.

explanations.answer: The great and awesome Day of the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, "The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD." (Joel 2:31) The signs come first, then the Day. It's why I keep my ovens ready, friend.

explanations.answer: The great harvest of the autumn rains
explanations.explanation: Harvest makes sense, since the passage's neighborhood is full of grain and rain. But the signs in the sky point somewhere else. The LORD says they come "before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD." (Joel 2:31) A dark sun is no harvest sign, friend.

explanations.answer: The return of the great locust army
explanations.explanation: I can see why the locusts crossed your mind, friend, because they ate a lot in this book. But the verse doesn't bring them back here. The sun turns to darkness and the moon to blood "before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD." (Joel 2:31) That Day is what the signs lead up to.

explanations.answer: Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The verse says, "And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved." (Joel 2:32) Everyone. Anyone who calls. That's a promise worth putting in a cookie box.

explanations.answer: Everyone who was born inside Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Jerusalem does show up in the verse, so I see the pull. But the verse says who will be saved, and it's not about where you were born. It says, "everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved." (Joel 2:32) The calling is the thing, friend.

explanations.answer: Everyone who never broke a single law
explanations.explanation: If that were the rule, friend, I'd be in trouble, and so would every stamper in my old junk drawer. But the verse doesn't say that. It says, "everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved." (Joel 2:32) Calling on His name is what the verse gives.

Remnant, baker! The verse says there will be deliverance "among the remnant called by the LORD." (Joel 2:32) A remnant is what's left, like the last few cookies in the bottom of the box. And these ones are called by the LORD.

Elders show up earlier in the book, so I see why you grabbed it. But in this verse the word is different. It says there will be deliverance "among the remnant called by the LORD." (Joel 2:32) Remnant is the word, friend.
Priests are a fair guess for a verse about Jerusalem. But that's not the word the LORD uses here. The verse says, "among the remnant called by the LORD." (Joel 2:32) Remnant is the answer, friend.
